newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi reviewing political reforms - King Fahd.
newsitem.headline: Saudi reviewing political reforms - King Fahd.

text.p: Saudi Arabia is examining how to develop political reforms introduced more than three years ago, King Fahd said in remarks published on Thursday.
The king made his comments in an interview published by the Saudi Okaz newspaper and its sister English-language Saudi Gazette.

Asked about the kingdom's Shura Council and regional assemblies, King Fahd said: "There is no system in the world that does not need revision or review for improvement. We are now in the process of reviewing the whole thing."

Stressing that Saudi Arabia was an Islamic country following Islamic laws, he said: "We spare no effort to seek the opinion and advice of the experts aiming to develop our systems in a way matching our principles and requirements."

King Fahd in 1993 set up a 60-member consultative council, the kingdom's first representative body for almost 60 years, and set up regional assemblies in 13 provinces, the first steps towards giving Saudis more say in running the country's affairs.
The Shura Council and the regional assemblies only have consultative powers.
Senior members of the royal family traditionally control the country's administration, occupying many top positions at national and provincial level.
The king, 75 this year, promised after the 1990-91 Gulf crisis to gradually introduce political and economic reforms aimed at modernising the system of government.
